Legal.mentionsBody:
Publisher

The LexGabon website is published as part of the ALIN initiative (Africa Law Innovation Network). The detailed legal information of the publishing entity (legal name, legal form, registered office, registration number) is being finalised. For any request, please write to the contact address below.

Contact
For any question relating to the site, its content or its services, please write to: contact@alin-africa.com.

Publication director
The publication director is the ALIN team. Individual identification is being formalised.

Hosting
The site is hosted by Vercel Inc., 340 S Lemon Ave #4133, Walnut, CA 91789, United States — https://vercel.com. The backend service (Ama'IA assistant and indexing) is hosted by Render, Inc. — https://render.com.

Intellectual property
Site elements (structure, text, graphics, logo, databases) are protected by intellectual property law. Any unauthorised reproduction is prohibited unless expressly stated otherwise. Official legal texts reproduced on the platform remain the property of their respective issuing authorities (Official Gazette of the Gabonese Republic, OHADA, CEMAC, COBAC, CIMA) and are made available for information and consultation purposes.

Personal data
Processing carried out via the site (including authentication, Ama'IA conversation history and browsing) is performed in accordance with applicable data protection law. You have rights of access, rectification, erasure and objection, which you can exercise by writing to contact@alin-africa.com. A detailed privacy policy will be published on this page in due course.

Liability
Legal content and information are provided for information only. They do not constitute legal advice and do not replace professional analysis. Only the text published by the issuing authority (Official Gazette or equivalent authentic source) is authoritative. The publisher cannot be held liable for any consequence arising from the use of the site's content without verification against the official source.
Legal.cguBody:
Purpose

These terms of use govern access to and use of the LexGabon website and related services, including the Ama'IA legal assistant.

Acceptance

Use of the site implies unreserved acceptance of these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.

User account

Some features may require an account. You agree to provide accurate information and to keep your credentials confidential. Activity carried out from your account is deemed to be yours.

Use of the service

You agree to use the site fairly, in compliance with applicable laws and without infringing third-party rights. The following are prohibited in particular: unauthorised access to systems, attempts to overload or alter the service, abusive automated use (unauthorised scraping, massive automated queries to the chatbot, etc.).

Ama'IA service

The Ama'IA assistant relies on generative AI models. Its responses may contain errors, omissions or inaccuracies and do not constitute personalised legal advice. You must systematically verify any information against official sources (Official Gazette of the Gabonese Republic, OHADA, CEMAC, COBAC, CIMA portals) and, where appropriate, consult a qualified professional. Ama'IA cites its sources when the document index allows; when no source is cited, additional caution is required.

Intellectual property and content

Editorial content, source code and databases remain the property of the publisher or its partners, subject to users' rights over their own data. Official legal texts reproduced on the platform remain the property of their respective issuing authorities.

Personal data

Processing is carried out in accordance with applicable data protection law. The data collected (session identifiers, Ama'IA conversation history, bookmarks) is used solely for the operation of the service. You can exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure and objection by writing to contact@alin-africa.com. A detailed privacy policy specifying legal bases, retention periods and recipients will be published in due course.

Changes to these terms

The publisher may amend these terms at any time. The applicable version is the one published on this page, together with the update date when provided. It is your responsibility to consult this page regularly.

Applicable law and disputes

These terms are governed by the law applicable at the publisher's registered office. In the event of a dispute, the parties shall endeavour to find an amicable solution before any judicial proceedings.

Methodologie.title: Methodology
Methodologie.intro: LexGabon is an open-access platform for the law applicable in Gabon. This page documents how our corpus is built, verified and maintained — so you can use our content confidently, and know exactly what we do and what we do not do.
Methodologie.principleBody: The Official Gazette of the Gabonese Republic or the authentic text published by the issuing authority is alone authoritative. LexGabon centralises, structures and makes these texts searchable; we do not create law, we make it accessible.
collectionItems: Manual download of the official PDFs published in the Official Gazette or by regional bodies (OHADA, CEMAC, COBAC, CIMA).
SHA-256 fingerprint verification to detect duplicates and ensure integrity.
Text extraction with automatic splitting by article (« Article N », « Art. N », variants including bis, ter, ordinals).
Concurrent indexing in a relational database (Postgres) for article-by-article display, and in a vector database (ChromaDB) for Ama'IA semantic search.
Targeted scraping of the official portals listed below, within a strict domain allowlist.
verificationItems: Per-text metadata maintained manually: code, authority, publication date, legal reference.
Regular corpus audit via the `verify_corpus.py` script: volume, distinct articles, alerts on missing metadata.
Systematic preservation of the link to the official source on every text record.
When a text is repealed, the record states so and points to the replacement version.
Methodologie.frequencyBody: The corpus is enriched on each relevant official publication. Automated monitoring runs daily at 03:00 UTC to spot new entries on monitored portals. Full code ingestions remain manual, triggered by our team.
engagementsItems: No generative AI is used to produce legal text. Ama'IA does not author law; it points to the applicable text and cites its sources.
No paywall, no forced sign-up to consult the corpus.
No advertising tracking, no third-party commercial cookies.
Ama'IA answers do not commit LexGabon or ALIN and do not constitute personalised legal advice.
Any factual statement produced by Ama'IA must be backed by an explicit citation; if the index does not supply a passage to cite, Ama'IA says so.
Methodologie.limitsBody: The corpus is being built. At this date, only the Gabonese Labour Code is fully ingested and indexed article by article. Other codes (civil, criminal, commerce, tax, electoral, Constitution) are being added. Searches in areas not yet indexed will return fewer results — Ama'IA states this in its response rather than fabricating a reference.
Methodologie.sourcesIntro: Only the official portals listed below are fetched by our scraping. No other domain is queried automatically.
Methodologie.corpusVolume: {chunks, number} indexed chunks · {articles, number} distinct articles
Methodologie.contactBody: If you spot an error in a text, a missing reference or a source we should add, write to the ALIN team — we promptly correct documented inaccuracies and publish the sources you flag when they fall within scope.

Apropos.metaDescription: Discover the mission of LexGabon, the ALIN team and our commitment to open access to Gabonese and regional law.
Apropos.title: About
Apropos.objectifBody: LexGabon is a digital platform dedicated to opening up access to Gabonese and regional law. It centralises legal texts from Gabon, as well as those of OHADA, CEMAC and COBAC, and offers AI-assisted exploration through Ama'IA, our conversational legal assistant.
Apropos.equipeIntro: LexGabon is led by a multidisciplinary team gathered around the African Legal Innovation Network initiative.
Apropos.mission1Body: For citizens, students and legal professionals — no paywall, no technical barrier.
Apropos.mission2Body: Legal publications from Gabon and the CEMAC zone, gathered in a single structured reference.
Apropos.mission3Body: Modern tools — semantic search, AI assistant — designed for everyday legal work.
Apropos.mission4Body: Modernise the regional legal landscape by making the law readable, verifiable and shareable.
